'Go again / At the beginning of your action phase, destroy this, then the next Guardian attack action card you play this turn gets +1{p}.' Guardian Action - Aura (MasteryPackGuardian). Blue printing of the family already drafted as .drafts/emerging_power_red.json (+3{p}) and .drafts/emerging_power_yellow.json (+2{p}); same skeleton, amount 1 per this batch's printed_text.

GO AGAIN NOT AUTHORED: GoAgain is in printed_keywords as an UNCONDITIONAL line of the text, so it fires from the card DB keywords field; re-authoring it would be a defect. No SOURCE_IS_ATTACK conditional-keyword machinery applies (nothing gates it).

TRIGGER: START_OF_ACTION_PHASE, not START_OF_TURN - 'at the beginning of your ACTION PHASE' is CR 4.3.1 wording and trigger_types.py:58 maps exactly that name (the corpus review files flag START_OF_TURN for this wording as wrong-timing). The engine listener dispatches it to the ACTIVE player's permanent zones including player.auras (engine.py:1514-1522), so the aura fires on its controller's own action phase - 'your action phase'; no IS_ACTIVE_PLAYER gate needed, same as the siblings.

EFFECT ORDER follows the printed sentence: DESTROY_SELF first (effect_types.py:2470 shares the DESTROY_PERMANENT branch; bare form destroys the source via canonical destroy(), which resolves the aura zone itself), then MODIFY_NEXT_ATTACK queues on the controller's dsl_queued_attack_mods (handler effect_types.py:4592+ READS mod/amount/filter/scope - verified this session). Destroying the aura first cannot unqueue the pump: the entry lives on the player, not the card. One-shot consumption by the first qualifying attack IS 'the next'; unused entries expire end of turn, which is 'this turn' (scope left at default TURN).

FILTER names 'Guardian attack action card': ATTACK_CLASS_IN reads 'classes' (Guardian is class/talent), ATTACK_TYPE_IN reads 'types' (Action), ATTACK_SUBTYPE_IN reads 'subtypes' (Attack) - keys verified against the handlers and against DSL_REFERENCE.md's MODIFY_NEXT_ATTACK filter table. The batch triage list named only the first two; the Attack-subtype term is kept for consistency with both sibling drafts, where it excludes non-attack Guardian actions.
